page: Amazon Web Services m8in.xlarge is an eighth-generation general purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at a nominal clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. The compute layer comprises 4 virtual CPUs partitioned across 2 physical cores utilizing 2 threads per core, backed by 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a standardized 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Architecturally designed for balanced workloads, the instance does not feature local storage volumes or discrete graphics processing units. Instead, storage operations rely fully on network-attached Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes, complemented by an integrated baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The architecture is suited for environments requiring consistent network throughput without the overhead of maintaining non-persistent local disks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8in.xlarge balances multi-threaded x86_64 processing density with an allocated network-enhanced profile. The balanced ratio of compute to memory delivers predictable resource allocation for general-purpose application stacks, containerized microservices, build pipelines, and mid-tier backend services that demand sustained 3.9 GHz processing performance without requiring extreme memory or local disk caching.

It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
